scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: This is the Office department (our PCs are on
192.168.3.x). All morning we have not been able to reach the Internet Lab
computers (the 128.168.0.x machines) -- everything over there just times out
for us, every single time. Other things are fine from here, so our machines
are working; the problem sits between us and the Internet Lab, and that is
your side. The network side is your job, not ours. Check what is wrong and
fix it today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No fault exists in the network. A thorough inspection of every layer on the Office-to-Internet-Lab path found the topology fully operational. All four Office hosts (192.168.3.x on lan_office) can reach all four Internet Lab hosts (128.168.0.x on lan_internet) with zero packet loss in both directions. Traceroute from office_pc to 128.168.0.2 confirms the expected three-hop forwarding path: the packet exits through router1 (192.168.3.1), crosses the 20.20.0.x WAN to router2 (20.20.0.2), and arrives at the Internet Lab — exactly as designed.

RIP v2 is converged on all three routers with complete and correct routing tables: router2 holds a valid RIP-learned route to 192.168.3.0/24 (metric 2 via router1), and router1 holds a valid route to 128.168.0.0/16 (metric 2 via router2). No distribute-lists, no passive-interface statements, and no iptables rules exist anywhere on the forwarding path. Every host has the correct IP address and default gateway. The FRR startup scripts on router0, router1, and router2 are all correctly configured.

The user's complaint that the Internet Lab is unreachable from the Office is not supported by any evidence in the live lab. The network is healthy. The issue was most likely a transient problem on the end-user side (e.g., a briefly disrupted container, ARP cache stale entry, or a temporary routing-convergence delay at lab startup) that has since self-resolved. No corrective action is needed on the network infrastructure.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies inter-router connectivity (traceroute shows packets crossing the 20.20.0.x WAN) and confirms router1 has a valid route to 128.168.0.0/16 and Office hosts reach Internet Lab hosts with 0% loss.

The agent's investigation logs show multiple successful pings, RIP/routes present, configs and iptables checked — supporting the conclusion that the path is healthy.
